evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible shared practice target, but the single state is composite
supporting_reason: Perfect HAVE plus a participial dependency recurs over 30 cells and has perfect-only, progressive-only, and joint perfect-progressive contrasts.
main_challenge: One state combines form, aspectual interpretation, auxiliary selection, and lexical participle knowledge across finite and modal chains; none of its 42 items is KC-isolating.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Matched semantic-choice and form-production items, crossed over lexical verbs and surrounding operator chains.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible shared practice target, but the single state is composite
supporting_reason: Progressive BE plus the -ing dependency recurs over 17 cells and is compositionally reused in perfect-progressive cells.
main_challenge: The state conflates progressive meaning, BE selection, -ing formation, and longer-chain ordering; none of its 29 items is KC-isolating.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Matched aspect-selection and form-realisation items across present, past, modal, passive, and perfect-progressive contexts.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: educationally recognisable target, but not established as one independently mastered operation
supporting_reason: Canonical BE-passive is a conventional pedagogical construction and recurs over 13 cells.
main_challenge: The declaration bundles argument remapping, auxiliary choice, and past-participle production; all 22 items also require another KC and lexical transitivity/participle knowledge is absent from the cell/Q representation.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Active/passive matched items with controlled verbs plus separate argument-structure and participle-form diagnostics.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible broad proficiency component, but too heterogeneous for an unqualified unitary mastery claim
supporting_reason: Past finite realisation recurs across 13 cells and has two simple-active isolating items.
main_challenge: The active cells span perfect HAVE, BE, DO-support, and lexical-main-verb contexts; the two isolating items use regular lexical past forms and do not isolate irregular or auxiliary knowledge.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Crossed regular/irregular lexical verbs and HAVE/BE/DO operator items, with tense-choice separated from inflection production.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible broad proficiency component, but too heterogeneous for an unqualified unitary mastery claim
supporting_reason: Present finite realisation recurs across 17 cells and has two simple-active isolating items.
main_challenge: The active cells span perfect HAVE, BE, DO-support, and lexical agreement; subject person/number is not represented and the isolating items only exercise third-person singular lexical -s.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Person/number-crossed lexical and auxiliary items, with tense-choice separated from agreement and allomorph production.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible pedagogical target, weakly and campaign-confounded in this bank
supporting_reason: Positive and negative imperatives are recognisable practice targets and the positive cell yields KC-isolating rows.
main_challenge: All four items come from the special bounded-chunk campaign, explicitly name imperative, and reduce to two narrow lexical patterns; the two positive items share the same target sentence.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Multiple deployable imperative formats and contexts, crossed with the same lexical material used in non-imperative controls.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: modal-lemma familiarity is plausible, but selection, meaning, and complement form are not separated
supporting_reason: The bank includes ability, negative inference/perfect, and polar-question contexts over four cells.
main_challenge: A single CAN state spans meaning/function and form, assumes no transfer from other modals, and 2/7 prompts literally provide CAN; the one isolating item is a simple ability sentence.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Uncued modal-choice items and common-form items crossed over ability, permission, and epistemic functions.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: not established as a unitary learnable competence
supporting_reason: COULD-specific performance can plausibly differ from other modal lemmas.
main_challenge: Five one-per-cell items span ability, impossibility, permission, and perfect/counterfactual-like uses; all five prompts literally supply COULD and three rely on rescue/intervention campaigns.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Uncued choice items stratified by modal function plus shared modal-complement form diagnostics.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: modal-lemma familiarity is plausible, but the declared selection KC is semantically mixed
supporting_reason: Eight items cover permission and epistemic possibility across simple, perfect, passive, negative, and question contexts.
main_challenge: Permission and epistemic uses are pooled; 5/8 prompts literally supply MAY and the single isolating item cannot establish general transfer.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Matched uncued MAY/MIGHT/CAN choice items by function and independent modal-plus-base form tasks.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: coherent within the sampled epistemic contexts, but measurement largely tests prompted form insertion
supporting_reason: The five items are relatively coherent around uncertain possibility over simple and perfect cells.
main_challenge: All five prompts literally supply MIGHT, two isolating items are near-parallel rain completions, and only three cells support the state.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Uncued probability/possibility choices and lexical/context diversity beyond the rain and retrospective-inference patterns.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: not established as one unitary competence
supporting_reason: MUST is an educationally salient modal lemma with seven items over five cells.
main_challenge: The bank pools obligation, prohibition, and epistemic deduction; 6/7 prompts literally supply MUST and only one simple positive item is isolating.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Function-stratified uncued modal choice, with obligation and deduction crossed over polarity, aspect, and voice.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible lemma knowledge, but register/function heterogeneity and sparse evidence make one state doubtful
supporting_reason: Four cells cover an offer, a formal rule, a polar offer, and progressive futurity.
main_challenge: All four prompts literally supply SHALL, each cell has only one item, and the contexts differ sharply in register and function.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Register-aware function labels, uncued alternatives, and replication within each retained SHALL use.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible modal family, but meaning and chain complexity are pooled
supporting_reason: The four items cover advice, retrospective regret, negated regret, and ongoing/progressive expectation.
main_challenge: Only one item is isolating, there is one item per cell, and a shared SHOULD state may hide distinct function and aspect burdens.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Repeated uncued advice/expectation/regret contrasts crossed with simple, progressive, and perfect forms.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible high-frequency form family, but the state bundles future use with chain and clause operations
supporting_reason: WILL has the broadest modal support: 14 items and nine cells across simple, question, progressive, perfect, and perfect-progressive contexts.
main_challenge: Only one item isolates WILL; six prompts literally provide it and four items required explicit-construction intervention, so apparent mastery can absorb chain difficulty and campaign style.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Crossed simple and complex forms with uncued future/volition/prediction contexts and explicit item/format effects.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: not established as one unitary competence
supporting_reason: WOULD-specific performance can plausibly differ from other modal lemmas and the bank contains a simple isolating row.
main_challenge: Five items pool polite willingness, counterfactual perfects, and reported speech; lexical identity alone does not justify equal transfer among these uses.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Function-labelled, uncued items that cross reported speech, requests/willingness, and counterfactuality with comparable forms.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible broad target, but the current one-state mechanism is strongly composite
supporting_reason: Negative polarity recurs broadly over 32 cells and 49 items.
main_challenge: No item isolates negation; active cells span DO-support, BE, perfect HAVE, and all nine modal operators, while the description claims DO insertion that only a subset requires; 24/49 prompts explicitly say negative/not or provide a negative form.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Operator-family-crossed polarity pairs and separate NOT placement versus DO-support diagnostics.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: linguistically plausible target, not independently supported by this inventory
supporting_reason: WH fronting plus question formation is an educationally recognisable operation.
main_challenge: Only one cell and two items exist; both are present negative DO-support questions, so the Q column is strictly nested in finite-present and negation and the state bundles WH fronting, inversion, and DO-support.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Positive/negative, present/past, auxiliary/modal, and multiple-WH-function cells plus a shared-inversion factor crossed with polar questions.

evidence_status: qualitative hypothesis, not expert or learner evidence
independent_improvability_judgment: plausible question-formation target, but current factorisation with WH questions is contestable
supporting_reason: Twelve items cover eight cells across DO-support, perfect HAVE, and six modal operators.
main_challenge: No item isolates the KC; every prompt necessarily cues a question task, and the declaration creates no shared operator-inversion state with non-subject WH questions despite the canonical operation inventory explicitly recognizing that shared mechanism.
discriminating_measurement_needed: Matched declarative/polar/WH transformations across the same operators, comparing shared-inversion plus WH-fronting against clause-type-specific states.
